title: Be patient, unlike the man of the fish
translation: So wait patiently for your Lord’s judgement, and do not be like the companion of the fish, who called out choked with distress. Had a grace from his Lord not reached him, he would have been cast onto the bare shore, blamed. But his Lord chose him and made him one of the righteous.
body: Jonah is named only as **“the companion of the fish”**; the story is assumed known. Ibn Kathir: he left his people **in anger**; with Ibn ʿAbbas and Mujahid he reads makẓūm as **“distressed”**. Jonah 2 gives the prayer itself. Luther, per Grislis: we must leap, **“trusting to God’s supporting and saving hand.”**
question: Verse 48 warns against being like Jonah “when he called out”. Was the fault his cry, or what came before it?
source_label: Ibn Kathir on 68:48 · Grislis, “Luther, Jonah, and the Leap of Faith” (1993)
reading: Egil Grislis, “Luther, Jonah, and the Leap of Faith,” Consensus 19:1 (1993)
